hero.heading: Stoller Dental Laboratory, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 3, 2026, from stollerdentallab.com, including the company history and products pages, and from public metal prices. No federal index is used, and this page says why. Every number is labeled; the assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $19,740 and $228,375), each rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display; the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Units you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per ten thousand units.

sliders.label: Share of units that carry metal
sliders.basis: Porcelain fused to metal, full cast, metal framework partials, and abutments; zirconia carries none. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Metal value in one metal-bearing unit
Units returned for remake
sliders.basis: Against a national average near 4 percent, per trade sources [[BENCHMARK]]. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Fully loaded cost of one remake
Metal value lost between bench and refiner
sliders.basis: Sprues and grindings sent back to the refiner, after its fees and float. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

constants.text: Metal uses the public gold price, $4,177 on October 1, 2026 against $3,864 a year earlier (+8.1 percent) [[BENCHMARK]]; gold's record in January 2026 is shown, not charged. Palladium $1,190, down 4.7 percent in a year. Zirconia has no public curve and is charged nothing.

model.disclosure: This model carries no federal index: none maps onto a dental laboratory.

terms.label: Metal drift inside a standing fee

model.formulaText: Moved per 10,000 units = 10,000 × metal share × metal value × 0.081 + 10,000 × remake share × remake cost + 10,000 × metal share × metal value × reclaim loss
model.plainText: In words, the slice of this year's gold rise a standing fee absorbs on the units that carry metal, plus the remakes doctors send back at their full cost, plus the metal value that slips away between the bench and the refiner.
model.callout: What nobody prices is the metal. Yours is the rare laboratory still casting gold and framing partials in alloy beside its zirconia mills, and a fee schedule stands for a year while gold rose 8.1 percent and touched its record in January; palladium went the other way, down 4.7 percent. A laboratory that bills metal at the day's market price prints it on the invoice; a standing fee absorbs the difference in silence. And the sprues and grindings that go back to the refiner settle at a price almost nobody checks after fees and float.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Your family founded the laboratory in 1977; you took the responsibility as president and, since 2021, as co-owner [[OBSERVED]].
Nearly half a century, every piece made in-house: restorations, removables, orthodontics, and implants, in a digital department and an analog one [[OBSERVED]].
Same-day repairs and temporaries. Complimentary pickup and delivery. A case any doctor can track online. A four-day week printed on the site [[OBSERVED]].
A product carrying your own name, Zircobites [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the count (four quarters of metal against the public prices and your settlements), the metal line in your own fee schedule, and the first month billed at the line, counted; fixed fee between $1,200 and $1,800; read-only; no patient information leaves the building.
